chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, from Sahib al-Askar (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We are brought something, and it is said, 'This is what was for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) with us.' So how should we deal with it?' He said: 'Whatever was for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) by reason of the Imamate, it is for me; and whatever was other than that, it is an inheritance according to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq depending on context, here referring to the predecessor)

ai.seo_question: How are the possessions of an Imam distributed between the current Imam and general inheritance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between the personal wealth of the Imams and the specific assets acquired through their unique status as 'Imamate' (such as the Khums or gifts given specifically to the office). This ruling establishes that while general possessions follow standard inheritance laws, items tied to the Imamate are retained by the succeeding Imam, reflecting the continuity of spiritual and administrative authority in Shia jurisprudence.
